verses.saheeh: When the Occurrence occurs,
verses.khattab: When the Inevitable Event takes place
verses.jalalayn: ﻿When the [imminent] Event comes to pass, [when] the Resurrection takes place,

verses.saheeh: There is, at its occurrence, no denial.
verses.khattab: then no one can deny it has come
verses.jalalayn: ﻿there will be no denying its coming to pass, [there is] no soul to deny [it], by repudiating it as it did in this world,

verses.saheeh: It will bring down [some] and raise up [others].
verses.khattab: It will debase ˹some˺ and elevate ˹others˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿[it will be] abasing [some], exalting [others], that is, it will manifest the abasing of some people by [virtue of] their admission into the Fire, and [manifest] the exalting of others by their admission into Paradise.

verses.saheeh: When the earth is shaken with convulsion
verses.khattab: When the earth will be violently shaken
verses.jalalayn: ﻿When the earth is shaken with a violent shock,

verses.saheeh: And the mountains are broken down, crumbling
verses.khattab: and the mountains will be crushed to pieces
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and the mountains are pulverised to [tiny] pieces,

verses.saheeh: And become dust dispersing.
verses.khattab: becoming scattered ˹particles of˺ dust
verses.jalalayn: ﻿so that they become a scattered dust (the second idh, ‘when’, is a substitution for the first idh),

verses.saheeh: And you become [of] three kinds:
verses.khattab: you will ˹all˺ be ˹divided into˺ three groups
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and you will be, at the Resurrection, three kinds, categories:

verses.saheeh: Then the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right?
verses.khattab: the people of the right, how ˹blessed˺ will they be
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Those of the right [hand], those who are given their record [of deeds] in their right hand (fa-ashābu’l-maymanati is the subject, the predicate of which is [the following mā ashābu’l-maymanati]) — what of those of the right [hand]? — a glorification of their status on account of their admittance into Paradise.

verses.saheeh: And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left?
verses.khattab: the people of the left, how ˹miserable˺ will they be
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And those of the left [hand] (al-mash’ama means al-shimāl, ‘left’), each of whom is given his record [of deeds] in their left hands — what of those of the left [hand]? — an expression of contempt for their status on account of their admittance into the Fire.

verses.saheeh: And the forerunners, the forerunners -
verses.khattab: and the foremost ˹in faith˺ will be the foremost ˹in Paradise˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And the foremost, in [the race to do] good, namely, the prophets (al-sābiqūna is a subject) the foremost: (this [repetition] is to emphasise their exalted status; the predicate [is the following, ūlā’ika’l-muqarrabūna])

verses.saheeh: Those are the ones brought near [to Allah]
verses.khattab: They are the ones nearest ˹to Allah˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿they are the ones brought near [to God],

verses.saheeh: In the Gardens of Pleasure,
verses.khattab: in the Gardens of Bliss
verses.jalalayn: ﻿in the Gardens of Bliss,

verses.saheeh: A [large] company of the former peoples
verses.khattab: ˹They will be˺ a multitude from earlier generations
verses.jalalayn: ﻿a multitude from the former [generations] (thullatun mina’l-awwalīna, the subject), that is to say, a group of individuals from communities of old,

verses.saheeh: And a few of the later peoples,
verses.khattab: and a few from later generations
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and a few from the later ones, from among the community of Muhammad (s), being the foremost from among the communities of old and this community (the predicate [is the following, ‘alā sururin mawdūnatin]),

verses.saheeh: On thrones woven [with ornament],
verses.khattab: ˹All will be˺ on jewelled thrones
verses.jalalayn: ﻿[will be] upon encrusted couches, [their linings] woven onto rods of gold and jewels,

verses.saheeh: Reclining on them, facing each other.
verses.khattab: reclining face to face
verses.jalalayn: ﻿reclining on them, face to face (muttaki’īna ‘alayhā mutaqābilīna constitute two circumstantial qualifiers referring to the [subject] person of the predicate [‘they’]).

verses.saheeh: There will circulate among them young boys made eternal
verses.khattab: They will be waited on by eternal youths
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They will be waited on by immortal youths, resembling young boys, never ageing;

verses.saheeh: With vessels, pitchers and a cup [of wine] from a flowing spring -
verses.khattab: with cups, pitchers, and a drink ˹of pure wine˺ from a flowing stream
verses.jalalayn: ﻿with goblets (akwāb are drinking-vessels without handles) and ewers (abārīq [are vessels that] have handles and spouts) and a cup (ka’s is the vessel for drinking wine) from a flowing spring, in other words, wine flowing from a spring that never runs out,

verses.saheeh: No headache will they have therefrom, nor will they be intoxicated -
verses.khattab: that will cause them neither headache nor intoxication
verses.jalalayn: ﻿wherefrom they suffer no headache nor any stupefaction (read yanzafūna or yanzifūna, [respectively derived] from nazafa or anzafa al-shāribu, ‘the drinker became inebriated’), in other words, they do not get a headache from it nor do they lose their senses, in contrast to [the case with] the wine of this world;

verses.saheeh: And fruit of what they select
verses.khattab: ˹They will also be served˺ any fruit they choose
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and such fruits as they prefer,

verses.saheeh: And the meat of fowl, from whatever they desire.
verses.khattab: and meat from any bird they desire
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and such flesh of fowls as they desire, for themselves to enjoy,

verses.saheeh: And [for them are] fair women with large, [beautiful] eyes,
verses.khattab: And ˹they will have˺ maidens with gorgeous eyes
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and houris, maidens with intensely black eyes [set] against the whiteness [of their irises], with wide eyes (‘īn: the ‘ayn here is inflected with a kasra instead of a damma because it [the kasra] better harmonises with the yā’; the singular is ‘aynā’, similar [in pattern] to hamrā’; a variant reading [for wa-hūrun ‘īn] has the genitive case wa-hūrin ‘īn)

verses.saheeh: The likenesses of pearls well-protected,
verses.khattab: like pristine pearls
verses.jalalayn: ﻿resembling hidden, guarded, pearls,

verses.saheeh: As reward for what they used to do.
verses.khattab: ˹all˺ as a reward for what they used to do
verses.jalalayn: ﻿a reward (jazā’an is an object denoting reason or a verbal noun, with the operator being an implicit [verb], in other words, ‘We have appointed for them the mentioned as a reward’ or ‘We have rewarded them [this]’) for what they used to do.

verses.uthmani: لَا يَسۡمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغۡوٗا وَلَا تَأۡثِيمًا
verses.indopak: لَا يَسْمَعُوْنَ فِيْهَا لَغْوًا وَّلَا تَأْثِيْمًاۙ
verses.transliteration: la yasma'oona feeha laghwan wala tatheeman
verses.saheeh: They will not hear therein ill speech or commission of sin -
verses.khattab: There they will never hear any idle or sinful talk—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They will not hear therein, in Paradise, any vain talk, any lewd words, or any sinful words,

verses.saheeh: Only a saying: "Peace, peace."
verses.khattab: only good and virtuous speech
verses.jalalayn: ﻿but only the saying, ‘Peace!’ ‘Peace!’ (salāman salāman substitutes for qīlan, ‘the saying’) which they will hear.

verses.saheeh: The companions of the right - what are the companions of the right?
verses.khattab: And the people of the right—how ˹blessed˺ will they be
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And those of the right [hand] — what of those of the right [hand]?

verses.saheeh: [They will be] among lote trees with thorns removed
verses.khattab: ˹They will be˺ amid thornless lote trees
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Amid thornless lote-trees, nabk trees,

verses.saheeh: And [banana] trees layered [with fruit]
verses.khattab: clusters of bananas
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and clustered plantains, banana trees, [weighed down] with its load [of fruit] from top to bottom,

verses.saheeh: And shade extended
verses.khattab: extended shade
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and extended shade, [one that is] permanent,

verses.saheeh: And water poured out
verses.khattab: flowing water
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and cascading water, running continuously,

verses.saheeh: And fruit, abundant [and varied],
verses.khattab: abundant fruit—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and abundant fruit,

verses.saheeh: Neither limited [to season] nor forbidden,
verses.khattab: never out of season nor forbidden—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿neither unavailable, during certain times, nor forbidden, because of [its] cost,

verses.saheeh: And [upon] beds raised high.
verses.khattab: and elevated furnishings
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and mattresses [that are] raised, on top of couches.

verses.saheeh: Indeed, We have produced the women of Paradise in a [new] creation
verses.khattab: Indeed, We will have perfectly created their mates
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Verily We have created them with an [unmediated] creation, namely, the wide-eyed houris, [We created them] without the process of birth,

verses.saheeh: And made them virgins,
verses.khattab: making them virgins
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and made them virgins, immaculate — every time their spouses enter them they find them virgins, nor is there any pain [of defloration] —

verses.saheeh: Devoted [to their husbands] and of equal age,
verses.khattab: loving and of equal age
verses.jalalayn: ﻿amorous (read ‘uruban or ‘urban, plural of ‘arūb, meaning ‘a woman passionately enamoured of her spouse’), of equal age (atrāb is the plural of tirb),

verses.saheeh: For the companions of the right [who are]
verses.khattab: for the people of the right
verses.jalalayn: ﻿for those of the right [hand] (li-ashābi’l-yamīni is the relative clause of [either] ansha’nāhunna, ‘We have created them’, or ja‘alnāhunna, ‘[We] made them’), who are:

verses.saheeh: A company of the former peoples
verses.khattab: ˹who will be˺ a multitude from earlier generations
verses.jalalayn: ﻿A multitude from the former [generations],

verses.saheeh: And a company of the later peoples.
verses.khattab: and a multitude from later generations
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and a multitude of the later ones.

verses.saheeh: And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left?
verses.khattab: And the people of the left—how ˹miserable˺ will they be
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And those of the left [hand] — what of those of the left [hand]?

verses.saheeh: [They will be] in scorching fire and scalding water
verses.khattab: ˹They will be˺ in scorching heat and boiling water
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Amid a scorching wind, an infernal wind, permeating the pores of skins, and scalding water, water of extreme temperatures,

verses.saheeh: And a shade of black smoke,
verses.khattab: in the shade of black smoke
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and the shade of pitch-black smoke,

verses.saheeh: Neither cool nor beneficial.
verses.khattab: neither cool nor refreshing
verses.jalalayn: ﻿neither cool, like all other shade, nor pleasant, [nor] agreeable in its appearance.

verses.saheeh: Indeed they were, before that, indulging in affluence,
verses.khattab: Indeed, before this ˹torment˺ they were spoiled by luxury
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Indeed before that, in the world, they used to live at ease, enjoying [life’s] comforts, never wearying themselves with [an act of] obedience,

verses.saheeh: And they used to persist in the great violation,
verses.khattab: and persisted in the worst of sin
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and they used to persist in the great sin, namely, idolatry.

verses.uthmani: وَكَانُواْ يَقُولُونَ أَئِذَا مِتۡنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابٗا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبۡعُوثُونَ
verses.indopak: وَكَانُوْا يَقُوْلُوْنَۙاَٮِٕذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا وَّعِظَامًا ءَاِنَّا لَمَبْعُوْثُوْنَۙ
verses.transliteration: wakanoo yaqooloona aitha mitna wakunna turaban wa'ithaman ainna lamab'oothoona
verses.saheeh: And they used to say, "When we die and become dust and bones, are we indeed to be resurrected?
verses.khattab: They used to ask ˹mockingly˺, “When we are dead and reduced to dust and bones, will we really be resurrected
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And they used to say, ‘What! When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected? (in both instances [a-idhā and a-innā] the two hamzas may be read either by pronouncing them fully, or by not pronouncing the second, and in either case inserting an intervening alif).

verses.saheeh: And our forefathers [as well]?"
verses.khattab: And our forefathers as well?”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿What! And our forefathers too?’ (read a-wa-ābā’unā, [with the wa-] being for supplement, the hamza [a-] for the interrogative; here and in the previous instance, it is used to express ‘remoteness [of probability]’; a variant reading has aw-ābā’unā, as a supplement with aw, and that to which this is supplemented is the [syntactical] locus of inna and its subject).

verses.saheeh: Say, [O Muhammad], "Indeed, the former and the later peoples
verses.khattab: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Most certainly, earlier and later generations
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Say: ‘Truly the former and the later [generations]

verses.saheeh: Are to be gathered together for the appointment of a known Day."
verses.khattab: will surely be gathered ˹together˺ for the appointed Day
verses.jalalayn: ﻿will be gathered for the tryst, the time, of a known day, that is, the Day of Resurrection.

verses.saheeh: Then indeed you, O those astray [who are] deniers,
verses.khattab: Then you, O misguided deniers
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then indeed you, the erring, the deniers,

verses.saheeh: Will be eating from trees of zaqqum
verses.khattab: will certainly eat from ˹the fruit of˺ the trees of Zaqqûm
verses.jalalayn: ﻿will assuredly eat from a Zaqqūm tree (min zaqqūm, the explication of shajar, ‘tree’),

verses.saheeh: And filling with it your bellies
verses.khattab: filling up ˹your˺ bellies with it
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and fill therewith, with the tree, your bellies,

verses.saheeh: And drinking on top of it from scalding water
verses.khattab: Then on top of that you will drink boiling water—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and drink on top of that, the consumed Zaqqūm, boiling water,

verses.saheeh: And will drink as the drinking of thirsty camels.
verses.khattab: and you will drink ˹it˺ like thirsty camels do.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿drinking like the drinking (read sharba or shurba: verbal noun) of thirsty camels’ (hīm is the plural of masculine haymān and feminine haymā, similar [in pattern] to ‘atshān, ‘atshā, ‘thirsty’).

verses.saheeh: That is their accommodation on the Day of Recompense.
verses.khattab: This will be their accommodation on the Day of Judgment
verses.jalalayn: ﻿This will be the hospitality for them, what has been prepared for them, on the Day of Judgement, the Day of Resurrection.

verses.saheeh: We have created you, so why do you not believe?
verses.khattab: It is We Who created you. Will you not then believe ˹in resurrection˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿We created you, We brought you into existence from nothing. Will you not then affirm [this] truth?, in resurrection? For the One able to create [from nothing] is also able to repeat [this creation].

verses.saheeh: Have you seen that which you emit?
verses.khattab: Have you considered what you ejaculate
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Have you considered the sperm that you emit?, the sperm you spill in the wombs of women?

verses.saheeh: Is it you who creates it, or are We the Creator?
verses.khattab: Is it you who create ˹a child out of˺ it, or is it We Who do so
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Is it you (a-antum: read by pronouncing both hamzas fully, or by replacing the second one with an alif or not pronouncing it, but inserting an alif between the one not pronounced and the other one, or without this [insertion] in the four instances [here and below]) who create it, that is, the sperm [making it] into a human being, or are We the Creators?

verses.uthmani: نَحۡنُ قَدَّرۡنَا بَيۡنَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمَسۡبُوقِينَ
verses.indopak: نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنَا بَيْنَكُمُ الْمَوْتَ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوْقِيْنَۙ
verses.transliteration: nahnu qaddarna baynakumu almawta wama nahnu bimasbooqeena
verses.saheeh: We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone
verses.khattab: We have ordained death for ˹all of˺ you, and We cannot be prevented
verses.jalalayn: ﻿We have ordained (read qaddarnā or qadarnā) death among you, and We are not to be outmanoeuvred from, We are not incapable [of],

verses.uthmani: عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ أَمۡثَٰلَكُمۡ وَنُنشِئَكُمۡ فِي مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
verses.indopak: عَلٰۤى اَنْ نُّبَدِّلَ اَمْثَالَـكُمْ وَنُـنْشِئَكُمْ فِىْ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُوْنَ
verses.transliteration: 'ala an nubaddila amthalakum wanunshiakum fee ma la ta'lamoona
verses.saheeh: In that We will change your likenesses and produce you in that [form] which you do not know.
verses.khattab: from transforming and recreating you in forms unknown to you
verses.jalalayn: ﻿replacing [you with], [We are not incapable of] appointing, your likes, in your place, and making you, creating you, in what you do not know, in the way of forms, such as apes or swine.

verses.uthmani: وَلَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتُمُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأُولَىٰ فَلَوۡلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
verses.indopak: وَلَـقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ النَّشْاَةَ الْاُوْلٰى فَلَوْلَا تَذَكَّرُوْنَ
verses.saheeh: And you have already known the first creation, so will you not remember?
verses.khattab: You already know how you were first created. Will you not then be mindful
verses.jalalayn: ﻿For verily you have known the first creation (al-nashā’ata: a variant reading has al-nash’ata), why then will you not remember? (tadhakkarūna: the original second tā’ [of tatadhakkarūna] has been assimilated with the dhāl).

verses.saheeh: And have you seen that [seed] which you sow?
verses.khattab: Have you considered what you sow
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Have you considered what you sow?, [what] you stir of the earth to place seeds therein?

verses.saheeh: Is it you who makes it grow, or are We the grower?
verses.khattab: Is it you who cause it to grow, or is it We Who do so
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Is it you who make it grow, or are We the Grower?

verses.uthmani: لَوۡ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ حُطَٰمٗا فَظَلۡتُمۡ تَفَكَّهُونَ
verses.indopak: لَوْ نَشَاۤءُ لَجَـعَلْنٰهُ حُطَامًا فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُوْنَ
verses.saheeh: If We willed, We could make it [dry] debris, and you would remain in wonder,
verses.khattab: If We willed, We could simply reduce this ˹harvest˺ to chaff, leaving you to lament
verses.jalalayn: ﻿If We will, We could surely turn it into chaff, dried vegetation producing no seed, and you would remain (zaltum is actually zaliltum, the lām having a kasra inflection; but it has been omitted to soften it), that is to say, you spend all day, bemused (tafakkahūna: one of the original tā’ [tatafakkahūna] letters has been omitted), surprised by this, and you would say:

verses.saheeh: [Saying], "Indeed, we are [now] in debt;
verses.khattab: “We have truly suffered a ˹great˺ loss
verses.jalalayn: ﻿‘We have indeed suffered loss!, [losing] what we expended on the cultivation.

verses.saheeh: Rather, we have been deprived."
verses.khattab: In fact, we have been deprived ˹of our livelihood˺.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nay, but we are deprived!’, prevented from [reaping] our provision.

verses.saheeh: And have you seen the water that you drink?
verses.khattab: Have you considered the water you drink
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Have you considered the water you drink?

verses.uthmani: ءَأَنتُمۡ أَنزَلۡتُمُوهُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُزۡنِ أَمۡ نَحۡنُ ٱلۡمُنزِلُونَ
verses.indopak: ءَاَنْـتُمْ اَنْزَلْـتُمُوْهُ مِنَ الْمُزْنِ اَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْزِلُوْنَ
verses.transliteration: aantum anzaltumoohu mina almuzni am nahnu almunziloona
verses.saheeh: Is it you who brought it down from the clouds, or is it We who bring it down?
verses.khattab: Is it you who bring it down from the clouds, or is it We Who do so
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Is it you who cause it to come down from the [rain] clouds (muzn is the plural of muzna) or are We the Causer of its coming down?

verses.uthmani: لَوۡ نَشَآءُ جَعَلۡنَٰهُ أُجَاجٗا فَلَوۡلَا تَشۡكُرُونَ
verses.indopak: لَوْ نَشَاۤءُ جَعَلْنٰهُ اُجَاجًا فَلَوْلَا تَشْكُرُوْنَ
verses.transliteration: law nashao ja'alnahu ojajan falawla tashkuroona
verses.saheeh: If We willed, We could make it bitter, so why are you not grateful?
verses.khattab: If We willed, We could make it salty. Will you not then give thanks
verses.jalalayn: ﻿If We willed, We could make it bitter, salty, undrinkable — why then will you not give thanks?

wbw.translation: then why are you not grateful?

verses.saheeh: And have you seen the fire that you ignite?
verses.khattab: Have you considered the fire you kindle
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Have you considered the fire that you kindle?, [the fire] which you produce out of the [oil of] green trees?

verses.uthmani: ءَأَنتُمۡ أَنشَأۡتُمۡ شَجَرَتَهَآ أَمۡ نَحۡنُ ٱلۡمُنشِـُٔونَ
verses.indopak: ءَاَنْتُمْ اَنْشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَهَاۤ اَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْشِـُٔـوْنَ
verses.transliteration: aantum anshatum shajarataha am nahnu almunshioona
verses.saheeh: Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer?
verses.khattab: Is it you who produce its trees, or is it We Who do so
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Was it you who created the tree thereof, [trees] such as the markh, the ‘afār or the kalkh [‘fennel’], or were We the Creator?

verses.saheeh: We have made it a reminder and provision for the travelers,
verses.khattab: We have made it ˹as˺ a reminder ˹of the Hellfire˺ and a provision for the travellers
verses.jalalayn: ﻿We made it a reminder, of the fire of Hell, and a boon, a provision, for the desert-travellers (al-muqwīn derives from [the expression] aqwā al-qawmu, ‘they have reached al-qawā or al-qawā’, that is, al-qafr, ‘desolate land’, which is a wilderness (mafāza) that has neither vegetation nor water).

wbw.translation: for the wayfarers in the desert.

verses.saheeh: So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
verses.khattab: So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Greatest
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So glorify, exalt the transcendence [of], the Name (ism is extra) of your Lord, the Tremendous, God.

verses.saheeh: Then I swear by the setting of the stars,
verses.khattab: So I do swear by the positions of the stars—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nay, I swear (fa-lā uqsimu: lā is extra) by the setting-places of the stars!

verses.saheeh: And indeed, it is an oath - if you could know - [most] great.
verses.khattab: and this, if only you knew, is indeed a great oath—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And indeed it, the swearing by these [setting-places of stars], is a tremendous oath, if you only knew — if you were people of [deep] knowledge, you would realise the magnitude of this oath.

verses.saheeh: Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an
verses.khattab: that this is truly a noble Quran
verses.jalalayn: ﻿This, namely, what is being recited to you, is indeed a noble Qur'an,

verses.saheeh: In a Register well-protected;
verses.khattab: in a well-preserved Record
verses.jalalayn: ﻿in a Book, inscribed, guarded, preserved, and this is the Mushaf;

verses.saheeh: None touch it except the purified.
verses.khattab: touched by none except the purified ˹angels˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿which none touch (lā yamassuhu is a predicate functioning as a prohibitive command) except the purified, those who have purified themselves of ritual impurities, [56:80] a revelation, revealed, by the Lord of the Worlds.

verses.saheeh: [It is] a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
verses.khattab: ˹It is˺ a revelation from the Lord of all worlds
verses.jalalayn: [It is] a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.

verses.saheeh: Then is it to this statement that you are indifferent
verses.khattab: How can you then take this message lightly
verses.jalalayn: Do you then belittle, [do you] take lightly and deny, this discourse?, the Qur'an.

verses.saheeh: And make [the thanks for] your provision that you deny [the Provider]?
verses.khattab: and repay ˹Allah for˺ your provisions with denial
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And for your livelihood, in the way of rain, that is to say, the thanks for it, you offer your denial?, of God’s granting it to you, by saying, ‘We have rain because of this [or that] storm’?

verses.saheeh: Then why, when the soul at death reaches the throat
verses.khattab: Why then ˹are you helpless˺ when the soul ˹of a dying person˺ reaches ˹their˺ throat
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Why then, when it, the spirit, during the throes [of death], reaches the [dying person’s] throat (hulqūm is the passage for food)

verses.saheeh: And you are at that time looking on -
verses.khattab: while you are looking on
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and you are, O you attending the dying person, at that moment looking, at him —

verses.uthmani: وَنَحۡنُ أَقۡرَبُ إِلَيۡهِ مِنكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُبۡصِرُونَ
verses.indopak: وَنَحْنُ اَقْرَبُ اِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ وَلٰـكِنْ لَّا تُبْصِرُوْنَ
verses.transliteration: wanahnu aqrabu ilayhi minkum walakin la tubsiroona
verses.saheeh: And Our angels are nearer to him than you, but you do not see -
verses.khattab: And We are nearer to such a person than you, but you cannot see
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and We are nearer to him than you are, to know [of his state], but you do not perceive (tubsirūna derives from al-basīra, ‘perception’) that is to say, you do not realise this —

verses.saheeh: Then why do you not, if you are not to be recompensed,
verses.khattab: Now, if you are not subject to Our Will ˹as you claim˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿why then, if you are not going to face a reckoning, [if] you are [not] going to be requited by your being resurrected, in other words, [why then, if] you are not going to be resurrected as you claim,

verses.saheeh: Bring it back, if you should be truthful?
verses.khattab: bring that soul back, if what you say is true
verses.jalalayn: ﻿do you not bring it back, [why] do you not restore the spirit to the body after it has reached the throat, if you are truthful?, in what you claim (the second law-lā, ‘why … if’, is [repeated] to emphasise the first one; idhā, ‘when’, is an adverbial particle qualifying tarji‘ūna, ‘bring it back’, to which both conditions are semantically connected). The meaning is: ‘Why do you not bring it back, when, in repudiating resurrection, you are being truthful in this repudiation?’ That is to say, ‘Let death also be repudiated [as impossible] in its case just as [you claim that] resurrection is [impossible]’.

verses.saheeh: And if the deceased was of those brought near to Allah,
verses.khattab: So, if the deceased is one of those brought near ˹to Us˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Thus if he, the dead person, be of those brought near,

verses.saheeh: Then [for him is] rest and bounty and a garden of pleasure.
verses.khattab: then ˹such a person will have˺ serenity, fragrance, and a Garden of Bliss
verses.jalalayn: ﻿then repose, that is, there will be for him relief, and a goodly provision, and a garden of Bliss (does this response belong to the ammā, ‘thus’, or to in, ‘if’, or to both? Different opinions [are given regarding this]).

verses.uthmani: وَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡيَمِينِ
verses.indopak: وَاَمَّاۤ اِنْ كَانَ مِنْ اَصْحٰبِ الْيَمِيْنِۙ
verses.transliteration: waamma in kana min ashabi alyameeni
verses.saheeh: And if he was of the companions of the right,
verses.khattab: And if the deceased is one of the people of the right
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And if he be of those of the right [hand],

verses.saheeh: Then [the angels will say], "Peace for you; [you are] from the companions of the right."
verses.khattab: then ˹they will be told,˺ “Greetings to you from the people of the right.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿then ‘Peace be to you’, that is, [then] for him there will be [peace by way of] security (salām) from chastisement, [a greeting] from those of the right [hand], [arising] from the fact that he is one of them.

verses.uthmani: وَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
verses.indopak: وَاَمَّاۤ اِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُكَذِّبِيْنَ الضَّاۤلِّيْنَۙ
verses.transliteration: waamma in kana mina almukaththibeena alddalleena
verses.saheeh: But if he was of the deniers [who were] astray,
verses.khattab: But if such person is one of the misguided deniers
verses.jalalayn: ﻿But if he be of the deniers, the erring,

verses.saheeh: Then [for him is] accommodation of scalding water
verses.khattab: then their accommodation will be boiling water ˹to drink˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿then a welcome of boiling water,

verses.saheeh: And burning in Hellfire
verses.khattab: and burning in Hellfire
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and a roasting in Hell-fire.

verses.saheeh: Indeed, this is the true certainty,
verses.khattab: Indeed, this is the absolute truth
verses.jalalayn: ﻿This indeed is the certain truth (haqqu’l-yaqīn: an example of an adjectivally qualified noun being annexed to its adjective).

verses.saheeh: So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
verses.khattab: So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Greatest
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Tremendous (as [explained] above [in verse 74]).
